Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Rounds 2 Determining Turn Order 3 The Turn 3.1 During their turn a player will do the following: 4 Planning Your Turn 4.1 Corners 4.2 Overtaking 4.3 Show Overspeed Alarm Option 5 Rolling Your Dice and Moving 5.1 Flat out: All the dice at once 5.2 One at a time 6 The Dice 7 Losing Control 7.1 Damage 7.2 Confirm Trajectory 8 Pit Stops 9 Flying Start 10 Tire Dashboards Rounds A game of Rallyman: GT is made up of alternating “white” and “black” rounds. Each player gets one turn each round. The Round marker has a white side and a black side, which allows you to immediately tell who has already played their turn this round. At the end of a round the Round marker is flipped over and a new round begins. Determining Turn Order At the beginning of each round, you must first determine the order of play. Order of play at the start of each round is determined by speed, then by the position of each car in case of a draw. SPEED > DISTANCE > POSITION Speed: Start by identifying the fastest car. The car with the highest Gear marker always plays first, no matter where they are on the track. Distance: If two or more cars are going at the same speed, then order of play is determined by how far along the track they are. The car furthest ahead plays first. Position: In case of a draw in terms of speed and distance, the car situated on the inside lane of the current or next corner plays first. A “corner” is a section of track with speed limitations. /* Note. The French rule book has been adopted in the BGA implementation. If cars are positioned in a corner, then the current corner is used for the evaluation, otherwise the next corner. */ The Turn Once order of play has been established, each player takes their turn one after the other. During their turn a player will do the following: Plan your turn. Roll your dice and move your car. Planning Your Turn During their turn, players will use dice to accelerate, brake, and coast their way around the track. Your player board (and the summary at the top of the screen) shows what dice are available to you. Each die number represents a gear. With each move you make, may go up or down one gear (or stay the same with a white die). You must always be moving forward. Each die may only be used once per turn. Corners Corner spaces have numbers in the middle which indicate the top gear in which you can safely navigate the corner. Exceed this number and you will lose control! The inside line: Some spaces have dotted lines separating them, with a lower number or caution symbol next to it. The number indicates the highest gear you can use to safely move between those spaces. Exceed it and you will lose control! The caution symbol gives one extra caution result when moving (see below) Note that you can safely move diagonally into spaces like this, as long as you don't exceed the normal limits. The outside line :Some spaces have a caution triangle around the number. This indicates that you get an extra caution result when you pass that space in that gear. Overtaking To enter a space adjacent to another player’s car, you must use a Gear die equal to or higher than the current Gear of the opponent’s car. Once your car is beside theirs, the rest of their movement can be at any speed. Note : if a yellow flag is out due to damage, you cannot overtake (move alongside) another player. [Rating: 1/10] KEEP FOR NOW  Kickstarter edition. real time rally game. Really different from the regular rallyman.

[Rating: 1/10] Just a big dice chugger, with no dept and extremely luck-driven system...if you hate luck driven games dont buy it... Although this game is a blast for people who just love to chug dice and dont care how little strategy is in this game... This games punish you for being first and if you crash in the beggining you have no chance of recovering and then you have to play through the entire game... Big fail for me...

[Rating: 1/10] Kickstarter all-in for Rallyman: Dirt and GT.  Never delivered due to incompetency and bankruptcy.

[Rating: 1/10] I don't understand this game. For me a frustratingly bad die roll is just a frustrating die roll.

[Rating: 1/10] Route planning rally exacerbating every race games shortcomings of previous decades (unforgiving, tedious, runaway leader, de facto elimination etc.) with, for the worst, a crawling and choking spin on 30 years old Formula Dé, losing a turn on a wide open track because the guy that pulled next to you is in nonsensical "higher gear"..

[Rating: 1/10] Just became a repetitive exercise of braking down from the highest gear to the lowest gear and reaccelerating back to the highest gear possible with every turn. The player that can 'math' out the best route to take and has the best luck with dice will win the game. See no point in playing it again. I dont mind luck in my games, hell, I think luck is important to prevent games from feeling samey and have those heroic moments (war-games like Risk where a single platoon holds off an entire battalion). But this game somehow manages to incorporate a luck-fest game that feels samey even with the wid

[Rating: 1/10] A push your luck dice based race game.   + Car pictures = nice! – Roll to move with obvious planning routes and extreme luck – Runaway leader – Player elimination/lose a turn!

[Rating: 1/10] Was a good game, unfortunately it was published by scammers, and Heat now absolutely crushes it in this space.  At this point it can be safely ignored forever.

[Rating: 1.4/10] Reading the rules it sounds good, but after more than 30 games I have to admit that this is just a luck-based dice game. The rules for turn order and especially blocking destroy the racing feeling. It is a push-your-luck game. So if you're unlucky with the dice, there's nothing you can do. For me personally, the luck factor is way too high. Also, the yellow flag rule is probably the dumbest rule they could have come up with. And the flying start also depends on the result of a single die.

[Rating: 2/10] I love racing games for their emotional ups and downs, amazing breakthroughs and surprising results.  This is a soulless game of moving you cars a few spaces forward, blocking each other and not going too fast. I hate it guts. And I haven’t even told you about humongous downtime!  Now - I am sure it brings the true spirit of car racing to the table - I will never ever watch a car race if it’s true. I do believe this is a great game for car racing fans - it just completely didn’t work with me and my expactations. I was frustrated and disapointed. The 2/10 is MY opinion, based on my feelings and

[Rating: 2/10] Roll to everything and if you roll bad miss a turn. I heard a bit of hype before I played so there's a fanbase, but everyone who played it hated it without me even making a comment.

[Rating: 2/10] Too dull and too slow for a racing game.   The movement puzzle is OK but the overall effect is too bland.  Actually - this is bad. Utterly boring and no fun.   If you are having a 'push your luck' game - make it fun. This is utterly tedious. There is no fun in 'pushing' - it's too punishing with the all-or-nothing rule.   Bad, bad game

[Rating: 2/10] You have an accident because a bad dice, an not only you are out of the game but also it takes forever until the next turn comes. Being out of the game right after you start to play is not fun...

[Rating: 2/10] I really enjoyed how [b][thing=60435][/thing][/b] captured rally car racing with its tracking time through cards and having the winner with the fastest time.  The whole space-for-time thing was delightful mental gymnastics.  Well, [b][thing=256589]Rallyman: GT[/thing][/b] got rid of my favourite part of the original game and replaced it with standard motor car racing.  Snore.

[Rating: 2/10] A push-your-luck game where getting lucky in a roll gives you currency to avoid rolling dice in future: unsurprisingly, this is a recipe for a runaway leader. It's also overly convoluted and too long, but it's the basic game design flaw that is the biggest problem.

[Rating: 2/10] Such an interesting premise, and a lot of the mechanics are a unique way of really bringing the car to life, but its penalties largely amount to missed turns, which simply kills most of the interest I have in playing it again. Which sucks, because I REALLY wanted to love this game.
